title: Two Spider-Man Minifigures From a Retiring LEGO Set Are Coming to the Marvel Magazine

bodyMarkdown:

Both figures reportedly come from **76324 Spider-Man vs. Oscorp**, a set that's said to be retiring at the end of 2026.

These aren't the most detailed versions of the two characters - other sets feature dual-moulded legs for extra detail - but Brick Fanatics notes they're an easy DIY upgrade if you fancy swapping in better legs later.

The report suggests this magazine issue follows a recent Hobgoblin-themed one, meaning UK shelves could see it within the next month or two. A typical price for these magazines with two free gifts has been around £7.99, though this isn't confirmed for the new issue.

If you're after these specific Spider-Man minifigure variants but don't want to buy the full Oscorp set or the Spider-Man vs. Venom Muscle Car set, this magazine could be a handy shortcut once it lands. It's also a reminder that 76324 Spider-Man vs. Oscorp is on its way out, so it's worth grabbing if you want it before it disappears from shelves.

## What to watch next

title: Great Western Brick Show Returns to Swindon Next Weekend
summary: The UK's longest-running LEGO fan show is back at STEAM – Museum of the Great Western Railway on 10–11 October, with hundreds of exhibitors and the popular Robot Battles event.
bodyMarkdown:
## What happened
The Great Western Brick Show, first held in 2002, returns to STEAM – Museum of the Great Western Railway in Swindon on 10 and 11 October. Brickset reports that more than 250 exhibitors, volunteers and traders will be taking part, with displays ranging from intricate railway layouts and cityscapes to castles, spacecraft, vehicles and engineering builds from UK and international builders.

A highlight of the weekend will be the 'Robot Battles', a format that began at the show in 2016 and has become one of its most popular attractions. More than 50 roboteers are expected to compete over the two days.

## Why it matters
For UK brick fans, this is one of the biggest chances of the year to see large-scale MOCs, custom builds and display techniques in person - great inspiration whether you're into stadium builds, cityscapes or collecting rare pieces. It's also a good opportunity to chat with experienced builders and pick up tips for your own projects.

## What to watch next

bodyMarkdown:

No official details of these 2027 sets have been revealed yet - no numbers, images or pricing. However, earlier rumours pointed to a wider range including polybags and larger builds referencing key Dragon Ball moments like Goku vs Raditz, the arrival on Namek, and a Kame House set. **These specific sets remain unconfirmed rumours** - only the existence of a broader 2027 wave has official backing so far.

## Why it matters
Dragon Ball is one of the biggest anime franchises worldwide, so official confirmation of an ongoing LEGO partnership is big news for both LEGO collectors and anime fans. It suggests LEGO Icons Shenron & Goku won't be a one-off collectible but the start of a proper licensed theme, similar to how LEGO expanded its KPop Demon Hunters sets.

## What to watch next
Keep an eye out for LEGO to officially reveal specific 2027 Dragon Ball sets, likely closer to launch. Until then, treat any leaked set numbers or images doing the rounds as rumour rather than confirmed fact.

summary: LEGO Marvel's Epic Moment Collection has completed its first full year with three display-friendly sets, and the upcoming 76348 Epic Battle: Avengers: Doomsday looks set to be the standout release yet.
bodyMarkdown:
## What happened
LEGO Marvel's newer Epic Moment Collection has reached the end of its first full year, according to Brick Fanatics. The range launched in January with two sets, 76334 Epic Battle: Spider-Man vs. Sandman (201 pieces) and 76343 Epic Battle: Hulkbuster vs. The Hulk (413 pieces), before a third model arrived nine months later.

That third set, 76348 Epic Battle: Avengers: Doomsday, is due to release on 1 October and is the largest of the trio at 846 pieces. It's based on the Avengers: Doomsday film and includes several exclusive minifigures, among them Mystique and Nightcrawler, alongside a more detailed Sentinel build.

All three sets share a tall, narrow design intended for desk display, meaning they can sit side by side without taking up much space. Fan builder Ashnflash has shown the trio together, showcasing Spider-Man, Iron Man and X-Men characters plus extra minifigures in one compact display.

## Why it matters
For UK LEGO Marvel fans and collectors, this is a useful snapshot of how a new, display-focused product line has developed over its debut year. The consistent design language across all three sets makes them easy to display together, which will appeal to anyone building out a Marvel shelf or cabinet. It's also a sign that LEGO may be leaning into smaller, characterful "moment" scenes rather than only large vehicle or building sets in this theme.

title: LEGO's Longest-Ever Set Wasn't Designed to Beat the Titanic
summary: The new UCS Executor Super Star Destroyer has overtaken the Titanic as LEGO's longest set ever, but its designer says that was never the plan.
bodyMarkdown:
## What happened
LEGO's new Ultimate Collector Series set, 75457 Executor Super Star Destroyer, measures a whopping 136cm long — just enough to edge out 10294 Titanic as the longest official LEGO set ever released.

According to designer John Ho, speaking in a roundtable interview with fan media including Brick Fanatics, this record wasn't the design team's goal. Instead, the length came down to part constraints. The engine section was based on an existing model, and the team had limited choices for scaling it — essentially certain Technic wheels or specific brick sizes. Once those fixed points were locked in, the rest of the ship's proportions followed, and the model ended up longer than intended.

In official marketing, LEGO has been careful to describe it as the longest Star Wars model rather than directly claiming the overall longest LEGO set title — even though it does now hold that record.

75457 Executor Super Star Destroyer launches for LEGO Insiders on 1 October, with a wider release on 4 October, priced at £649.99 / €749.99 / $799.99. Buyers who purchase between 1–7 October will get a free 40897 Darth Vader's Lightsaber gift with purchase while stocks last.

## Why it matters
For UCS collectors and display builders, this is a genuinely fascinating look behind the curtain — showing how real engineering and part limitations, not marketing targets, can shape a flagship model's final scale. It's also a useful reminder for anyone planning shelf space: at 136cm, this set needs serious display real estate.
